name: Exp A: Search-question long-forms (practical tirzepatide)
hypothesis: Long-forms on practical 'get the most from tirzepatide' questions people search (strength training, protein, side effects, stopping) will beat approved-drug deep dives (median 8) and keep gaining views over time. Strength Training (48, still climbing at day 9) is the model.
change: Lane A runs on no-news, no-decoder days (2–3 this week): practical tirzepatide topics only, searched phrase first, about 60 characters or fewer, at most 1 number. Cost, coverage and timeline-only topics are excluded from now on. Slot, length and retention rules stay the same.
metric: Views at day 7 and day 28. Success: day-7 median of 25 or more and still growing at day 28. Once the API is on, also average view duration and watch hours per video.
min_sample: n=8 videos to call it (about 11-03 to 11-05). Judge each video at day 7 and day 28.
result: Interim, below target. In-window logged: How Long 26, What to Eat 11 (day 4), Medicare 3 (day 2): median 11, n=3. Side Effects (10-24) isn't logged yet. Including Strength Training from before the experiment (48): median 18.5, n=4. Cost topics are removed from the lane after Medicare got 3 (anecdote).

name: Exp B: Gray-market 'what's actually confirmed' long-forms
hypothesis: Our strongest Short lane (gray-market 'what's confirmed?', median about 105, n=7) would also work as long-form.
change: 2 long-forms a week in lane B, credited and dated, no sellers named.
metric: Day-7 views compared with the GLP-1 long-form median. Success: day-7 median of 33 or more.
result: Closed early at n=1. 'Semaglutide or Tirzepatide Online: How to Check a Pharmacy' got 6 views by day 3. That's an anecdote and doesn't prove the lane fails. We're stopping because each slot costs a probable Lane A or C video (medians 18.5 and 47), and the lane sits close to 'online sources' policy risk. Gray-market stays a Shorts-only lane (at most 1 a week). Any retest has to go through Lane C with a fresh dated FDA, MHRA or manufacturer event.

name: Exp C: First explainer within 48 h of a newly named drug or result
hypothesis: Being the first clear explainer of a new named result with little search competition (EloraTZP 523) drives long-form views far more than any title formula.
change: When a named next-gen drug's result or regulatory step first becomes public within 48 h, that day's long-form explains it with the drug name first in the title. Qualifying news goes to the long-form before any Short. A journal publication of an old topline counts only if it adds new data.
metric: Day-7 views compared with the GLP-1 long-form median (20, n=17) and approved-drug deep dives (8). Success: day-7 median of 50 or more.
min_sample: n=4 qualifying videos made after 10-20 (probably 2–4 weeks, depending on news).
result: In-window n=1: petrelintide (10-25), not logged yet; score it at day 7 on 11-01. Looking back at earlier fresh-news next-gen long-forms: median 47 (n=5: 523, 56, 47, 25, 18), a signal. Missed this week: two next-gen news topics (retatrutide sleep apnea, retatrutide kidneys) went to Shorts and were both dropped for masking. Note: TRIUMPH-1 OSA results were first announced on 6 Jun 2026, so the radar must check the first-report date before calling anything 'new'.

name: Exp D: Shorts-to-long-form funnel with a verified link
hypothesis: A funnel Short that asks a fresh question its live long-form answers will lift that long-form's daily views when it ends by naming the exact title and carries a working, verified link. Shorts average about 60 YouTube views each and currently send no measurable traffic to long-form.
change: Every 20:00 Short is a spin-off of a live long-form, rotating between that day's Lane C video, EloraTZP and Strength Training on Tirzepatide. Last spoken line: 'Full breakdown: [exact live title], on our channel.' The oEmbed-verified URL goes in description line 1 and the pinned comment. Only the presence of the working link and CTA changes; topic rules stay the same.
metric: The target long-form's views in the 3 days after the Short against the 3 days before (from daily snapshots). Once the API is on, use 'Shorts feed' and 'related video' traffic sources. Success: average lift of 10 or more views a day, or 50% or more over the baseline.
min_sample: n=6 funnel Shorts with a verified working link. Shorts that ship without a verified link are excluded.
result: Started 2026-10-26. Baseline: no Short has ever shipped with a working long-form link. EloraTZP and Strength Training are each gaining roughly 1–3 views a day.
